sides.name: Sweden and Saxony (Gustavus Adolphus, John George I)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 40,150 (22,800 Swedes, 17,350 Saxons; Cristini) and 66 guns. Infantry (pike and shot combined; Swedish ~2:1 shot:pike) vs cavalry split is an educated guess. Weapons 5.3: light regimental guns and salvo fire. Training 0.65 = blend of Swedes (~0.85) and newly raised Saxons (~0.35) who fled at the start. Command 0.9: Gustavus Adolphus. riverCrossing false: no contested river crossing, the armies met on open ground north of Leipzig (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Breitenfeld_(1631)).

sides.name: Holy Roman Empire and Catholic League (Tilly)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 31,400 (14,700 Imperial, 15,700 League, 1,000 irregulars; Cristini), 27 guns (Mankell). Other estimates up to ~35,000. Infantry in tercios; cuirassiers/harquebusiers as cavalry_heavy, Croats as cavalry_light (split is an educated guess). Mapped to archetype-gunpowder-linear (no tercio doctrine in the list). Command 0.6: Tilly experienced, but Pappenheim charged without orders. prepared false: Tilly stood on the Galgenberg without field works and his side took the offensive (Pappenheim's charges, the tercios' advance on the Saxon position) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Breitenfeld_(1631)).

outcome.note: Swedish-Saxon victory. Swedish-Saxon 5,550 killed or wounded (3,550 Swedish, 2,000-3,000 Saxon). Imperial-League 7,600 killed or wounded + 6,000 captured; high includes stragglers and losses at Leipzig in the pursuit. Artillery from about noon, fighting ended at nightfall (~21:00).
